# attention.productions

Each address is a shot, written as an image prompt.

The path is the subject, a hyphen is a space, and each ladder is a query key whose value is one of its words (hyphens for spaces). What the address leaves out, the date picks; day=2026-12-01 fixes a date; tempo=0.5..2 scales motion speed (rest 1).

- shot: extreme close-up, close-up, medium, wide, establishing, overhead, low angle
- lens: 24mm, 35mm, 50mm, 85mm, macro, anamorphic
- light: golden hour, raking dawn, noon, overcast, window light, lamplight, candlelight, sodium night, neon
- from: above, left, right, below, behind
- move: still, dolly-in, handheld, rack focus, long exposure
- ratio: square, portrait, photo, widescreen, scope, vertical
- focus: center, left third, right third, upper third, lower third
- tempo: 0.5 to 2 in steps of 0.1 (default 1; drawn on the viewfinder bar and written as %tempo[n] in Spw)
- material: any of texture.website's 91 listed material words (its /vocabulary.json); the prompt then carries --sref with that material's image from texture.website and --sw 250.
- wear, process: texture.website's own surface words (wear: pristine, handled, worn, weathered, ruined; process: as found, riso, engraving, relief, posterized, cyanotype); left out, the prompt says nothing of either.
- A neighbour's word is read as the nearest word here (raking sun as raking dawn, 100mm as macro, near as the lower third); light=backlight is from=behind.

The page supports inline subject editing, draggable viewfinder handles (focus ring, lamp, tempo bar), horizontal bracket scrubbing across the Spw expression, a six-take A/B comparison strip, and a three-shot storyboard beat (establishing, medium, close-up) that opens directly on factshift.center via #spw64=.

The page writes a Midjourney prompt (--ar in whole numbers, so scope is 239:100; https://docs.midjourney.com/aspect-ratios), a plain prompt for any model, and Spw lines:
  !shot[close-up]{a laminated folio}(lamplight)<85mm>
  ^frame{ =ratio[scope] =focus[left_third] =light_from[right] ~move[still] %tempo[1] }
  @material: ~"texture.website/vellum.spw"

Example: https://attention.productions/a-laminated-folio?shot=close-up&lens=85mm&light=lamplight&from=right&move=dolly-in&ratio=scope&focus=left-third&material=vellum

Readings: /vocabulary.json (ladders, phrases, ratios), /ecosystem.json (the set), https://texture.website/llms.txt (materials), https://factshift.center/ (spatial canvas), https://spw.quest/llms.txt (Spw grammar).
